questions.question: Which event is considered the turning point in Gandhi’s political life, converting him from a moderate to a mass leader?

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha (1917)** marked the **first instance of Gandhi’s active involvement in Indian politics**. It was a pivotal event where Gandhi transitioned from a moderate reformer to a mass leader.
 
• The agitation was aimed at addressing the plight of the **indigo farmers** in Champaran district, Bihar, who were subjected to exploitative practices by British planters.
 
• Gandhi employed his strategy of **non-violent civil disobedience** for the first time in India during this movement, inspiring widespread participation and support from the masses. *Hence, Champaran Satyagraha was a turning point in Gandhi’s political life.*
 
• It established Gandhi’s leadership and laid the foundation for his future movements based on the principles of **truth, non-violence, and satyagraha**.
 
• Gandhi’s success in resolving the farmers’ grievances demonstrated his ability to mobilize people, connect with grassroots issues, and challenge British authority. This was a significant shift in his approach to Indian politics. *Hence, statement is correct.*

• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919):**

 
 
• This tragic event involved the killing of **hundreds of unarmed civilians** by British troops under General Dyer’s orders.

questions.question: In which year did French physicist Sadi Carnot create the Carnot engine, which uses thermodynamic principles to function as an ideal heat engine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1824**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sadi Carnot**, a French physicist and engineer, is often regarded as the "Father of Thermodynamics" due to his groundbreaking contributions to the field.
 
• In **1824**, Carnot published a seminal work titled *"Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire"*, in which he introduced the concept of the **Carnot engine**. This engine represents an idealized heat engine that operates on reversible processes.
 
• The **Carnot engine** is based on the principles of **thermodynamics**, particularly the idea of maximizing efficiency by minimizing energy waste. Carnot’s model became fundamental to understanding heat transfer and energy conversion.
 
• Carnot explained that no engine working between two heat reservoirs can be more efficient than a Carnot engine, and its efficiency depends solely on the temperature difference between the reservoirs.
 
• This concept laid the foundation for the **Second Law of Thermodynamics**, which governs the direction of heat flow and energy transformation. *Hence, the year 1824 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Sadi Carnot:**

 
 
• **Sadi Carnot** was born in **1796** in France. He is best known for his work on the theoretical aspects of heat engines, which contributed significantly to the field of thermodynamics.
 
• His work emphasized the importance of **reversible processes** in achieving maximum efficiency in heat engines, setting the stage for advancements in energy systems.
 
 
 
• **The Carnot Engine:**
 
 
• The **Carnot engine** is a theoretical construct that operates in a closed cycle, consisting of four reversible stages: two isothermal processes and two adiabatic processes.
 
• It demonstrates the maximum efficiency achievable by a heat engine, which depends on the **temperature difference** between the heat source and the heat sink.
 
• **Example:** Modern heat engines, such as steam turbines and refrigeration systems, are designed based on the principles outlined in Carnot's work.
 
 
 
• **Second Law of Thermodynamics:**
 
 
• Carnot's work directly contributed to the development of the **Second Law of Thermodynamics**, which states that heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
 
• This law also establishes the concept of entropy, which measures the level of disorder or randomness in a thermodynamic system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Efficiency of the Carnot Engine:**

 
 
• The efficiency of a Carnot engine is determined by the formula *η = 1 - (T꜀ₒₗd / Tₕₒₜ)*, where **Tₕₒₜ** and **T꜀ₒₗd** are the temperatures of the heat source and sink, respectively.
 
• This formula highlights the impact of temperature difference on the engine’s performance.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Carnot’s Work:**
 
 
• Carnot's ideas influenced the development of practical heat engines and the understanding of energy efficiency.
 
• His work forms the basis of modern thermodynamics and continues to guide engineers in optimizing energy systems.

• **The Paris Agreement** is a global climate accord adopted in **December 2015** during the **21st Conference of the Parties (COP21)** in **Paris, France**.
 
• Its primary goal is to limit the increase in **global average temperature** to well below **2° Celsius** above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit the temperature rise to **1.5° Celsius**.
 
• This agreement is legally binding, meaning countries that are party to it are obligated to take action to meet their commitments. *Hence, statement is correct.*

• The pursuit of the more ambitious **1.5° Celsius** target aims to further reduce risks associated with climate change, particularly for **vulnerable countries** and populations. *Hence, the correct temperature limit is 2° Celsius.*

questions.question: Which authority is the appellate body under the RTI Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Information Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Information Commission (CIC):** The **Central Information Commission** is the designated appellate authority under the **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005**. It addresses grievances and resolves disputes related to RTI requests.
 
• The CIC is responsible for ensuring transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities by adjudicating appeals and complaints filed under the RTI Act.
 
• The commission functions as an independent body and has the authority to summon public officials, review documents, and order disclosure of information if required. *Hence, the correct answer is Central Information Commission.*
 
• **Structure of the CIC:** The commission consists of the **Chief Information Commissioner** and up to ten **Information Commissioners**, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners have a tenure of **five years** or until they reach the age of **65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• **Role in RTI:** The CIC acts as a final appellate authority to hear appeals against decisions made by the Public Information Officer (PIO) or the First Appellate Authority in cases where applicants are dissatisfied with the responses received.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Information Act, 2005:**

 
 
• The **RTI Act** was enacted to promote transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities.
 
• It gives citizens the right to access information held by public authorities, subject to certain exemptions and conditions.
 
• The act applies to all levels of government—**Central, State, and local bodies**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Central Information Commission:**
 
 
• The CIC adjudicates on appeals and complaints related to RTI applications, ensuring compliance with the RTI Act.
 
• It has the power to direct public authorities to take necessary actions, such as providing information or justifying its denial.
 
• The CIC can impose penalties on public officials for non-compliance or delay in providing information.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Commissioners:**
 
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners are appointed by the President of India based on recommendations by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister.
 
• This ensures that the commission operates independently and impartially.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exemptions under RTI Act:**

 
 
• Certain sensitive information is exempted from disclosure under the RTI Act, including matters related to **national security, sovereignty, and integrity of India.**
 
• Information prohibited by **courts of law** or relating to commercial confidence, trade secrets, or intellectual property is also exempted.
 
 
 
• **Other Authorities Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Chief Vigilance Commission:** This authority deals primarily with vigilance and corruption cases in government offices and does not have a role in RTI appeals.
 
• **National Human Rights Commission:** The NHRC addresses issues related to human rights violations and does not serve as the appellate authority under the RTI Act.
 
• **Lokpal:** Lokpal is an anti-corruption ombudsman that investigates complaints of corruption against public officials. It is not involved in RTI appeals.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut allows you to select multiple specific files or folders at once?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + Click**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ctrl + Click** shortcut allows users to select multiple specific files or folders. This is useful when the files are not adjacent to each other and need to be selected individually.
 
• Using **Ctrl + Click** ensures that the selection is additive, meaning that each additional click adds to the already selected items without deselecting others. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Tab + Click** is not used for selecting multiple files; it is typically used for navigation between fields or elements in applications. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Alt + Click** is not a standard shortcut for selecting multiple files; it is often used for specific actions in software (e.g., selecting objects in design software). *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Shift + Click** allows users to select a range of files that are adjacent to each other. However, it is not suitable for selecting non-adjacent files. *Hence, this statement is correct in a different context.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functionality of Ctrl + Click:**

 
 
• The **Ctrl key**, when held down, allows users to make multiple selections without overriding previous selections.
 
• It is commonly used in **Windows File Explorer** or macOS Finder to select multiple files or folders that are spread across different positions.
 
 
 
• **Shift + Click Usage:**
 
 
• While **Shift + Click** is used to select a range of items, it is limited to selecting items that are adjacent to each other.
 
• For example, if you click the first file, hold **Shift**, and click the last file, all files in between will be selected.
 
 
 
• **Tab Key Usage:**
 
 
• **Tab + Click** is not a valid shortcut for file selection. The **Tab key** is primarily used for navigation between fields or interactive elements.
 
• For example, pressing **Tab** allows users to move to the next field in a form or navigate through buttons and menus.
 
 
 
• **Alt Key Usage:**
 
 
• The **Alt key** is generally used for accessing menus and shortcuts specific to particular software, not for file selection.
 
• In some applications like graphic design software, **Alt + Click** allows advanced selection techniques, but it does not apply to regular file selection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Ctrl + Click:**

 
 
• It enables users to select specific items without affecting the selection of others, making it flexible and efficient.
 
• This shortcut is particularly useful when working with large datasets or organizing files.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Operating Systems:**
 
 
• **Windows OS:** The **Ctrl key** is widely used for multiple selections in File Explorer and other applications.
 
• **macOS:** The equivalent shortcut in macOS is **Command + Click**, serving the same purpose for selecting multiple files.

questions.question: What defines land as “Culturable Wasteland” in land revenue records in India?

options.text: Land that is fallow for over five years

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Land that is fallow for over five years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Culturable Wasteland:** In India, land recorded as "Culturable Wasteland" in revenue records refers to land that is **capable of cultivation** but has not been used for agricultural purposes for a prolonged period, specifically for **more than five years.**
 
• This category of land includes areas that have the potential for agricultural production but have been left uncultivated due to various reasons, such as **poor soil quality, lack of irrigation facilities, or socio-economic issues.**
 
• The classification of "Culturable Wasteland" ensures that such land is identified for possible reclamation and use in agricultural development programs.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is "Land that is fallow for over five years."*
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Urban infrastructure land:** This type of land is utilized for development purposes, such as construction of buildings, roads, and other urban facilities. It does not qualify as "Culturable Wasteland" because it is not suitable for agriculture.
 
• **Land under tree crops:** Land with tree crops is already in use for cultivation, particularly for horticulture or forestry. It cannot be categorized as wasteland.
 
• **Barren rocky land:** This type of land is unsuitable for cultivation due to its rocky terrain and poor soil quality. It is categorized separately and does not fall under "Culturable Wasteland."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Land Classification in India:** The land in India is categorized into various types based on its usage and productivity:

 
 
• **Cultivable Land:** Land that is actively used for agricultural purposes.
 
• **Culturable Wasteland:** Land that is arable but has been left uncultivated for a long time, typically for over five years.
 
• **Barren and Uncultivable Land:** Land that cannot be used for agriculture due to poor soil quality, rocky terrain, or other physical limitations.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Culturable Wasteland:**
 
 
• Such land can be reclaimed for agricultural production by improving soil fertility, providing irrigation, and addressing socio-economic challenges.
 
• It can also be used for plantation, forestry, or other sustainable practices to enhance its productivity.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**

• The **National Wasteland Development Board (NWDB)** was established in **1985** to identify and utilize wasteland effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• They help in planning land use, implementing agricultural policies, and managing resources effectively.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Culturable Wasteland in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Reclaiming such land can contribute significantly to increasing agricultural productivity in India.
 
• It is vital for achieving food security and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

questions.question: The drain of wealth theory was a major critique of colonial economic policies. Who propounded the ‘Drain of wealth theory’ in the late 19th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**, also known as the "Grand Old Man of India," propounded the **Drain of Wealth Theory** in the late 19th century.
 
• The theory stated that the **British colonial rule in India** led to the systematic transfer of wealth and resources from India to Britain.
 
• This theory was first articulated in Naoroji's book titled **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"**, published in **1901**.
 
• Naoroji highlighted that the colonial policies drained India's **economic resources**, leading to widespread **poverty** and stagnation among Indians.
 
• He identified various mechanisms through which wealth was drained, such as **home charges**, salaries for British officials in India, and the profits earned by British companies operating in India.
 
• Naoroji argued that this drain of wealth was the primary reason for India's **economic backwardness** during colonial rule.
 
• The Drain of Wealth Theory became a cornerstone for economic critiques of British imperialism and influenced the early **Indian nationalist movement**.
 
• Other leaders like **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** and **Mahatma Gandhi** also acknowledged Naoroji's contributions and expanded upon his ideas in their struggle against colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:**

 
 
• **Born:** In **1825** in Bombay (now Mumbai), India.
 
• **Profession:** An educator, political leader, and one of the first Indian members of the **British Parliament**.
 
• **Significance:** Naoroji was instrumental in laying the foundation for economic nationalism in India and advocating for Indian rights.
 
 
 
• **The Drain of Wealth Mechanisms:**
 
 
• **Home Charges:** Payments made by India to Britain for administrative expenses, military costs, and pensions for British officials.
 
• **Trade Policies:** India was used as a supplier of raw materials for British industries and a market for British goods, adversely affecting Indian industries.
 
• **Salaries:** High salaries and profits paid to British officials and traders working in India drained wealth from the country.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Theory:**
 
 
• The Drain of Wealth Theory raised awareness among Indians about the exploitative nature of British colonialism.
 
• It became a key argument for Indian nationalists demanding **economic and political independence**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Contributions of Dadabhai Naoroji:**

 
 
• Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the **British House of Commons** in **1892**.
 
• He played a significant role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in **1885**.
 
• His book, **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"**, provided a detailed analysis of the economic impact of British policies on India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Naoroji's ideas inspired future leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Jawaharlal Nehru** in their fight for India's independence.
 
• He is considered one of the pioneers of modern economic thought in India.

questions.question: Which of the following architectural styles is predominantly associated with the Gateway of India in Mumbai?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Saracenic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gateway of India:** The Gateway of India, located in Mumbai, is a historic monument that was built to commemorate the visit of **King George V** and **Queen Mary** to India in **1911**. Its construction was completed in **1924**.
 
• The architectural style of the Gateway of India is predominantly **Indo-Saracenic**, which is a blend of traditional Indian architectural elements and **Islamic, Gothic, and Neoclassical styles**.
 
• The monument is made of **basalt and reinforced concrete**, featuring intricate detailing, arches, and domes, which are hallmarks of the Indo-Saracenic style.
 
• The central dome of the Gateway of India is about **26 meters high** and is flanked by intricately designed honeycomb-like lattice stonework, reflecting traditional Indian craftsmanship.
 
• This architectural style was widely used during the British colonial era in India and represents a blend of **Indian and Western architectural influences**.
 
• The Gateway of India is one of the most iconic landmarks in Mumbai and serves as a symbol of India’s rich heritage and colonial history.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Indo-Saracenic.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Saracenic Architecture:**

 
 
• **Indo-Saracenic architecture**, also known as Indo-Gothic, is an architectural style that emerged during British colonial rule in India. It combines elements of **Indian, Islamic, and Western Gothic** architectural styles.
 
• It often features **domes, arches, minarets, and intricate ornamentation** influenced by Mughal and Hindu architectural traditions, along with elements of Gothic revival and Victorian architecture.
 
• Examples of Indo-Saracenic architecture in India include the **Gateway of India**, the **Victoria Memorial** in Kolkata, and the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Art Deco Architecture:**
 
 
• **Art Deco** is a modernist architectural style that originated in the early 20th century and is characterized by **geometric patterns, bold colors, and luxurious materials**.
 
• Mumbai is home to a significant number of Art Deco buildings, particularly along Marine Drive and the Oval Maidan.
 
• However, the Gateway of India is not an example of Art Deco architecture.
 
 
 
• **Bauhaus Architecture:**
 
 
• The **Bauhaus style** originated in Germany during the early 20th century and is characterized by **minimalism, functionality, and modern industrial materials**.
 
• This architectural style emphasizes simplicity and rejects unnecessary ornamentation, which is quite different from the intricate design of the Gateway of India.
 
 
 
• **Victorian Gothic Architecture:**
 
 
• The **Victorian Gothic** style, popular during the 19th century, features pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses, inspired by medieval Gothic architecture.
 
• In Mumbai, the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** is a prime example of Victorian Gothic architecture, but the Gateway of India does not fall into this category.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Construction of the Gateway of India:**

 
 
• The foundation stone for the Gateway of India was laid in **March 1913**, and the structure was completed in **1924**.
 
• It was designed by the British architect **George Wittet**, who combined elements of **Hindu, Islamic, and European architectural styles**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Indo-Saracenic Style:**
 
 
• The Indo-Saracenic style was widely used in colonial India, as it blended local architectural traditions with Western influences, symbolizing the **fusion of cultures**.
 
• The style was often used for public and government buildings, including railway stations, courthouses, and memorials.

questions.question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court of India impose a three-month deadline for the President to give assent to State Bills reserved under Article 201?

options.text: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980)
SR Bommai vs. Union of India (1994)
State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)
Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in the landmark case of **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)**, imposed a **three-month deadline** for the President to decide on State Bills reserved for consideration under **Article 201**.
 
• **Article 201** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the procedure for assent to bills reserved by the **Governor** for the consideration of the President. The President may either give assent or withhold assent to the bill.
 
• This judgment emphasizes the importance of preventing undue delays in the assent process for bills passed by state legislatures and reserved for the President's consideration. *Hence, this is the correct case.*
 
• This decision is significant in maintaining the federal structure of India, ensuring that the states' legislative processes are not hindered by indefinite delays in decision-making.
 
• The Supreme Court's ruling provides clarity on the procedure and timelines for decisions related to state bills, promoting accountability and efficiency in governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 201 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 201** empowers the President to either give assent to a bill reserved by the Governor or withhold assent.
 
• The article is designed to ensure that bills passed by state legislatures align with the central laws and policies. However, it does not specify any time frame for the President's decision, leading to delays in some cases.
 
• The Supreme Court's ruling in **2023** sets a precedent by introducing a **three-month deadline** for the President to decide, ensuring better legislative efficiency.
 
 
 
• **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023):**
 
 
• This case highlights the issue of delays in decision-making regarding bills reserved under **Article 201.**
 
• The judgment reinforces the principle of cooperative federalism, ensuring that state legislations are not indefinitely stalled.
 
• It serves as a benchmark for similar cases in the future, bringing clarity to the process of granting assent to state bills.
 
 
 
• **Other Landmark Cases:**
 
 
• **Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980):** This case dealt with the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles but did not address Article 201.
 
• **SR Bommai vs. Union of India (1994):** This case focused on the application of President's Rule and federalism, not Article 201.
 
• **Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973):** This case was pivotal in establishing the Basic Structure Doctrine but did not involve Article 201.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Significance:**

 
 
• The judgment in **State of Tamil Nadu vs. Governor of Tamil Nadu (2023)** underscores the importance of timely decision-making in the legislative process.
 
• By imposing a **three-month deadline**, the Supreme Court ensures that governance at the state level is not compromised due to procedural delays.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Federalism:**
 
 
• The case strengthens the concept of **cooperative federalism**, where both the Center and States work in harmony without undue interference.
 
• It provides a clear framework for handling bills under **Article 201**, fostering trust and transparency between the state and central authorities.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced a cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** introduced a cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers.
 
• According to this amendment, the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the State Council of Ministers cannot exceed **15% of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly**.
 
• This amendment was enacted to ensure efficient governance and to curb unnecessary expansion of ministries, which could lead to financial burdens and administrative inefficiencies.
 
• The amendment also introduced provisions for disqualification of legislators under the **anti-defection law**, strengthening the political structure and promoting accountability.
 
• The **anti-defection law**, added as the **Tenth Schedule** of the Constitution, was amended to ensure that defecting legislators lose their right to hold any ministerial position.
 
• This amendment applies to both the Union Council of Ministers and the State Council of Ministers, bringing uniformity to the structure and size of government across the country.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:**

 
 
• This amendment was implemented to promote efficient governance and reduce the financial burden caused by oversized councils of ministers.
 
• It introduced a **mandatory cap of 15%** on the size of councils of ministers at both the central and state levels.
 
• It strengthened the **anti-defection law** by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial positions, ensuring political stability.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Defection Law:**
 
 
• Added to the Constitution as the **Tenth Schedule** by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985**.
 
• It seeks to prevent political defections by disqualifying members of the legislature who switch parties.
 
• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act** further strengthened this law by including provisions to disqualify defectors from holding ministerial positions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 91st Amendment:**
 
 
• Promotes **transparent governance** by limiting the size of councils of ministers.
 
• Ensures financial prudence by reducing unnecessary expenditure on salaries and allowances for ministers.
 
• Encourages political accountability by preventing defectors from being rewarded with ministerial positions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background of the 91st Amendment:**

 
 
• Before the 91st Amendment, there was no cap on the size of councils of ministers, leading to excessive expansion and inefficiencies.
 
• The amendment was introduced in response to growing concerns about governance inefficiencies and financial burdens caused by oversized ministries.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Amendments:**
 
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:** Introduced provisions for **Panchayati Raj**, establishing a three-tier system of governance at the local level.
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988:** Reduced the **minimum voting age** from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and state assembly elections.
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:** Known as the **Mini Constitution**, it brought significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of the words **“Socialist” and “Secular”** to the Preamble.

questions.question: Which irrigation method is considered most efficient for water conservation in agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drip Irrigation**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drip irrigation** is considered the most efficient irrigation method for conserving water. It delivers water directly to the root zone of plants through small emitters, minimizing water wastage.
 
• This system significantly reduces **evaporation** and **runoff**, ensuring that plants receive only the required amount of water.
 
• Drip irrigation systems are ideal for areas with **low water availability** or **arid regions**, as they use water more effectively compared to traditional methods like flood or furrow irrigation.
 
• The method enhances **soil health** by preventing waterlogging and ensuring consistent moisture levels, which leads to better crop yield.
 
• Drip irrigation systems are highly suitable for **greenhouses, orchards, vineyards**, and vegetable farms, where precise water application is critical.
 
• Although the initial installation of a drip irrigation system can be **costly**, its long-term benefits in terms of water conservation and crop yield outweigh the investment.
 
• This method also allows for the efficient application of **fertilizers** and nutrients by mixing them with water, reducing waste and ensuring targeted nourishment of crops.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Furrow Irrigation:**

 
 
• **Furrow irrigation** involves creating shallow channels along the field where water flows to irrigate crops. While it is less costly and easier to implement, it leads to significant **water loss** due to evaporation and runoff.
 
• This method is suitable for crops like maize, sugarcane, and cotton, but it is less efficient compared to drip irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Flood Irrigation:**
 
 
• **Flood irrigation** involves flooding the entire field with water. It is one of the oldest methods but is highly **inefficient**, as a large quantity of water is wasted due to evaporation and seepage.
 
• This method is primarily used for crops like rice, but it can lead to waterlogging and soil erosion, affecting the crop yield negatively in the long term.
 
 
 
• **Sprinkler Irrigation:**
 
 
• **Sprinkler irrigation** involves spraying water over crops through overhead sprinkler systems. While it is more efficient than furrow or flood irrigation, it still leads to water loss due to **evaporation**.
 
• Sprinkler systems are suitable for crops like cereals, vegetables, and lawns, but they are not as precise or water-conserving as drip irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Drip Irrigation:**
 
 
• Drip irrigation can save up to **30-50%** of water compared to conventional methods like flood irrigation.
 
• It reduces weed growth since water is applied only to the root zones, minimizing moisture in other areas.
 
• This system enhances the efficiency of fertilizer application, reducing costs and environmental impact.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Benefits:**

 
 
• Drip irrigation helps conserve water resources and minimizes soil erosion, making it a sustainable choice for agriculture.
 
• It reduces the risk of water contamination due to reduced runoff, which is beneficial for protecting nearby water bodies.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct longitudinal extent of the Prime Meridian?

__
 
• **Prime Meridian:** The Prime Meridian is the longitudinal line designated at **0° longitude**. It serves as the starting point for measuring longitude around the globe.
 
• It is also known as the Greenwich Meridian because it passes through the **Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London**.
 
• The Prime Meridian divides the Earth into two hemispheres: the **Eastern Hemisphere** and the **Western Hemisphere**. This makes it a significant reference point in geography.
 
• The longitudinal extent of the Prime Meridian is measured as **0°**, and it is used as the basis for the **Global Coordinate System.**
 
• The Prime Meridian is universally accepted as the reference for calculating **time zones**, with **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)** being based on this meridian.
 
• Other options mentioned in the question, such as **90° E, 180° E,** and **23.5° N**, refer to different coordinates on Earth. They do not represent the Prime Meridian, which is always 0° longitude. Hence, these options are incorrect.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 0°.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prime Meridian History:**

 
 
• The concept of the Prime Meridian was formalized during the **International Meridian Conference** in **1884** in Washington, D.C.
 
• It was decided that the meridian passing through the **Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London**, would be the global Prime Meridian.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Prime Meridian:**
 
 
• It serves as the reference line for measuring longitude, which ranges from **0° to 180°** east and west.
 
• The Prime Meridian is crucial in defining **time zones**. The time at the Prime Meridian is referred to as **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).**
 
• It helps in determining the **International Date Line**, which is located at 180° longitude.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Greenwich:**
 
 
• Greenwich was chosen as the location for the Prime Meridian due to its historical importance in navigation and astronomy.
 
• The **Royal Observatory**, established in **1675** by King Charles II of England, played a pivotal role in advancing maritime navigation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Longitude and its Measurement:**

 
 
• **Longitude** is measured in degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian, ranging from **0°** at the Prime Meridian to **180°**.
 
• Longitude lines are used in conjunction with latitude lines to define **coordinates** for any location on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Other Meridians:**
 
 
• **90° E:** Refers to the longitude passing through eastern Asia, including parts of India and China.
 
• **180°:** Refers to the **International Date Line**, which serves as the opposite side of the Prime Meridian.
 
• **23.5° N:** Refers to the latitude of the **Tropic of Cancer**, not a longitude.

• **Satyagraha Sabha** was founded by **Mahatma Gandhi** on **24 February 1919** to oppose the **Rowlatt Act**.

• **Rowlatt Act:**

 
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, also known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was passed by the British Government to curb growing nationalist activities. It gave the government extensive powers to arrest and detain individuals without trial.

• **Satyagraha Movement:**
 
 
• **Satyagraha** is a concept of non-violent resistance developed by Mahatma Gandhi. It involves using truth and non-violence as tools to fight injustice and oppression.
 
• The **Satyagraha Sabha** was an organization created to implement and spread the principles of Satyagraha across India. It played a crucial role in mobilizing masses against British policies.

• The protest against the **Rowlatt Act** culminated in the infamous **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** on **13 April 1919**, where British troops under General Dyer opened fire on unarmed civilians in Amritsar.
 
• This tragic event significantly intensified the Indian freedom struggle and led to greater participation in Gandhi's non-cooperation movement.

questions.question: Why are soft drink and soda water bottles sealed under high pressure in beverage industries?

options.text: To decrease the amount of sugar
To increase the solubility of carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the solubility of carbon dioxide.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soft drink and soda bottles** are sealed under high pressure specifically to enhance the **solubility of carbon dioxide (CO₂)** in the liquid. Under high pressure, CO₂ dissolves more efficiently, creating the fizzy texture that is characteristic of carbonated beverages.
 
• At lower pressures, carbon dioxide escapes from the liquid, leading to a loss of the signature fizz and carbonation. Hence, sealing under high pressure ensures long-lasting carbonation. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The process of sealing bottles under high pressure is an application of **Henry's Law**, which states that the amount of gas dissolved in a liquid is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas above the liquid. *Hence, this principle supports the practice in beverage industries.*
 
• Soft drink companies use this technique to maintain the desired taste, as the dissolved CO₂ contributes to the tangy taste and fizzy sensation. Without sealing the bottles under pressure, the drink would lose its flavor and appeal. *This is an important factor for customer satisfaction.*
 
• Other options mentioned in the question, such as increasing temperature, preventing freezing, or decreasing the amount of sugar, are irrelevant to the carbonation process. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Henry's Law:**

 
 
• **Henry's Law** states that the amount of gas that dissolves in a liquid is proportional to the pressure of the gas in contact with the liquid. This is why soft drink manufacturers utilize high pressure to dissolve CO₂ effectively.
 
• When the bottle is opened, the pressure is released, and CO₂ escapes in the form of bubbles, creating the fizz that we enjoy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Carbonation:**
 
 
• **Carbonated beverages** like soda, sparkling water, and soft drinks rely on this process to enhance taste and texture.
 
• The carbonation process also plays a role in beverages such as **beer** and **champagne**, where natural fermentation creates CO₂.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Pressure:**
 
 
• High-pressure sealing ensures **long-term storage** of carbonated drinks without losing their fizz.
 
• It also prevents microbial growth as CO₂ creates an acidic environment, extending the shelf life of the beverage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• Increasing the temperature does not contribute to carbonation. In fact, higher temperatures reduce CO₂ solubility.
 
• Preventing freezing is not relevant to soft drink bottling under pressure. Freezing is controlled through storage conditions.
 
• Decreasing the amount of sugar is unrelated to the carbonation process. Sugar content is determined by the recipe for taste.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• **Beverage manufacturers worldwide** use similar techniques to preserve the fizz in carbonated drinks, adhering to industry standards.
 
• The use of CO₂ in beverages is regulated by food safety authorities like the **FDA** in the **United States** and **FSSAI** in **India**.

• The **British East India Company** was founded on **31st December 1600** through a royal charter granted by Queen Elizabeth I.

• The company initially traded in **spices**, which were highly valued in Europe during that era. Over time, its focus shifted to other goods, including textiles, tea, and opium.
 
• By the early 17th century, the British East India Company had begun establishing trading posts and factories in India, marking the beginning of British commercial influence in the region.
 
• In the subsequent centuries, the company transitioned from being a commercial entity to a colonial power, eventually leading to the establishment of British rule in India.
 
• The founding of the company in **1600** laid the groundwork for later British dominance over India, which culminated in the establishment of the British Raj in **1858**.

• The company was created to compete with other European powers, such as the **Portuguese** and the **Dutch**, who were already active in the Indian Ocean trade.

• By the **1750s**, the company had its own army and began to take control of large territories in India, including **Bengal**, after the famous **Battle of Plassey** in **1757**.
 
 
 
• **Transition to British Rule:**
 
 
• The British East India Company's administrative control over India ended with the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, after which the British Crown took direct control of the Indian territories.
 
• The company was formally dissolved in **1874**, but its legacy shaped the socio-economic and political landscape of modern India.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is guaranteed under Article 25 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Right to move the Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to freedom of religion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 25** of the **Indian Constitution** guarantees the **Right to Freedom of Religion** to all citizens of India. This right is fundamental for ensuring religious liberty.
 
• It provides individuals the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate their religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• The Article ensures that the State does not interfere in religious practices unless necessary to maintain public order or safeguard other constitutional provisions. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Article 25** also protects the rights of religious groups to manage their own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• The provision ensures that religious practices are safeguarded but also allows the State to regulate or restrict practices that may conflict with social welfare or the rights of others. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Key Limitations:** The freedom of religion under Article 25 is not absolute. It is subject to **public order, morality, health**, and other provisions of Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The State can also regulate non-religious aspects of religious practices that have economic, political, or social implications. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Right to freedom of religion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 25 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• **Article 25** is one of the most significant provisions for ensuring religious freedom in India. It provides individuals the right to freely practice their religion, subject to certain restrictions.
 
• The Article also protects the rights of religious groups and communities to manage their own affairs in matters related to religion.
 
 
 
• **Other Articles Related to Religious Freedom:**
 
 
• **Article 26:** Provides every religious denomination the right to manage its religious affairs.
 
• **Article 27:** Prohibits the use of taxpayer money for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
 
• **Article 28:** States that no religious instruction shall be provided in educational institutions funded by the State.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Article 25:**
 
 
• The freedom extends to individuals and groups of all religions.
 
• It ensures equal treatment of all religions and prohibits discrimination based on religion.
 
• Allows the State to regulate religious practices that may conflict with other constitutional principles, such as social welfare or public order.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Considerations:**

 
 
• Article 25 ensures religious freedom but imposes restrictions to maintain **public order, morality, and health**.
 
• The State can regulate or restrict practices that infringe upon the rights of others or conflict with social welfare.
 
 
 
• **Notable Judicial Interpretations:**
 
 
• **Shirur Mutt Case (1954):** The Supreme Court held that religious practices are protected under Article 25, but only those practices considered essential to the religion.
 
• **Azan Case (2020):** The court ruled that the use of loudspeakers for religious purposes is not an essential religious practice and can be regulated.

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities has zero dimension in mass and time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volume** is a physical quantity that measures the three-dimensional space occupied by an object or substance.
 
• It is represented mathematically as the product of length, width, and height.
 
• The formula for calculating volume for a rectangular object is **Volume = Length × Width × Height**.
 
• In terms of dimensions, volume is expressed as **L³**, where **L** represents length.
 
• It has **zero dimensions** in mass and time since its dimensions are only related to length and not to mass or time. *Hence, the correct answer is Volume.*
 
• Other quantities such as **Force**, **Work**, and **Momentum** involve mass and/or time in their dimensional formulas.
 
• For instance, force is expressed as **MLT⁻²**, work as **ML²T⁻²**, and momentum as **MLT⁻¹**, indicating their dependency on mass and time. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Dimensions:**

 
 
• **Dimensions** are used to express the dependence of a physical quantity on fundamental quantities such as mass (**M**), length (**L**), and time (**T**).
 
• For example, the dimensional formula of force is **MLT⁻²**, indicating its dependency on mass, length, and time.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Volume:**
 
 
• **Volume** is a scalar quantity, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction.
 
• It is measured in cubic units such as **cubic meters (m³)**, **liters (L)**, or **milliliters (mL)**.
 
• Volume is commonly used to measure liquids, gases, and solid objects in various fields such as **engineering**, **medicine**, and **construction**.
 
 
 
• **Other Physical Quantities:**
 
 
• **Force:** It is the interaction that causes an object to move or change its motion. Its SI unit is **Newton (N)**.
 
• **Work:** Work is done when force is applied to an object, causing displacement. Its SI unit is **joule (J)**.
 
• **Momentum:** It is the product of mass and velocity, representing the quantity of motion an object possesses. Its SI unit is **kg·m/s**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Understanding Dimensional Analysis:**

 
 
• Dimensional analysis is a mathematical tool used to check the correctness of physical equations and relationships.
 
• It is based on the principle that dimensions of all terms in a physical equation must be consistent.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Volume measurement is essential in industries like **chemical engineering**, **civil engineering**, and **medicine**.
 
• It is used for calculating the capacity of containers, determining the amount of liquid or gas stored, and assessing storage requirements.

questions.question: The sum of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 34. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest odd natural numbers are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

Their respective squares are 1, 9, 25, 49, 81.

By observation, the sum of adjacent squares 9 and 25 is exactly 34 (9 + 25 = 34).

Thus, the two consecutive odd numbers are 3 and 5.

Required sum = 3 + 5 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sum of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 34.

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

Let the two consecutive odd natural numbers be x and x + 2.

⇒ x² + (x + 2)² = 34

⇒ x² + (x² + 4x + 4) = 34

⇒ 2x² + 4x + 4 − 34 = 0

⇒ 2x² + 4x − 30 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ x² + 2x − 15 = 0

Factorizing the quadratic equation:

⇒ x² + 5x − 3x − 15 = 0

⇒ x(x + 5) − 3(x + 5) = 0

⇒ (x − 3)(x + 5) = 0

⇒ x = 3 or x = −5

Since the given numbers are natural numbers, x must be positive. So, x = 3.

The second consecutive odd number is x + 2 = 3 + 2 = 5.

Sum of the numbers = 3 + 5 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Odd Numbers

The difference between any two consecutive odd numbers is always 2. The general form of an odd natural number is 2n − 1, where n is a natural number.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd natural numbers is always equal to a perfect square, given by n².

Quadratic Roots Nature

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are real and distinct if the discriminant (D = b² − 4ac) is greater than 0.
</p

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

67, 75, 81, 70, 65, 61, 65, 84, 75, 76, 85, 89, 62, 84, 72, 74, 89, 68, 83, 60, 82, 82, 66, 77, 75
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a given dataset.

Instead of counting all numbers, we can save time by checking the frequencies of the given options only.

Count from the data: 81 → 1 time, 70 → 1 time, 67 → 1 time.

Count from the data: 75 → 3 times.

Since 75 appears the maximum number of times among all options, it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dataset: 67, 75, 81, 70, 65, 61, 65, 84, 75, 76, 85, 89, 62, 84, 72, 74, 89, 68, 83, 60, 82, 82, 66, 77, 75

**Formula Used:**

Mode = The observation that occurs with the highest frequency in a given dataset.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us systematically count the frequency of the repeated numbers in the dataset to find the mode.

⇒ The number 65 appears exactly 2 times.

⇒ The number 82 appears exactly 2 times.

⇒ The number 84 appears exactly 2 times.

⇒ The number 89 appears exactly 2 times.

⇒ The number 75 appears exactly 3 times.

⇒ All the other remaining numbers appear only 1 time each.

⇒ The maximum frequency in the entire dataset is 3, which corresponds to the number 75.

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean

The arithmetic average of a dataset. Formula: Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Median

The middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order. For an even number of observations (n), it is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th and (n ÷ 2 + 1)th terms.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by the formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Bimodal Dataset

A dataset that contains two distinct values with the same highest frequency is called bimodal. In such distributions, there are two separate modes.
</p

The difference between each divisor and its remainder is consistently 2 (3 − 1 = 2, 5 − 3 = 2, 9 − 7 = 2).

This means that (Required Number + 2) must be perfectly divisible by all the divisors (3, 5, 7, and 9).

Using the divisibility rule of 9, let us check which option + 2 gives a sum of digits divisible by 9:

Option 1: 999808 + 2 = 999810 → Sum of digits = 27 (Divisible by 9)

Option 2: 999998 + 2 = 1000000 → Sum of digits = 1 (Not divisible by 9)

Since only Option 1 satisfies this condition, we can immediately identify the correct answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 999808.**

Remainders = 1, 3, 5, and 7

Required Number = (Largest 6-digit multiple of LCM) − k

Where k is the common difference between the divisors and their respective remainders.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Common difference (k) = 3 − 1 = 5 − 3 = 7 − 5 = 9 − 7 = 2

⇒ LCM of 3, 5, 7, and 9 = 315

⇒ Largest 6-digit number = 999999

⇒ Divide 999999 by 315: 999999 ÷ 315 = 3174 with a remainder of 189

⇒ Largest 6-digit multiple of 315 = 999999 − 189 = 999810

⇒ Required Number = 999810 − k

⇒ Required Number = 999810 − 2 = 999808

**∴ The correct answer is 999808.**

A number is completely divisible by 9 if the sum of its individual digits is a multiple of 9. This rule is highly efficient for eliminating incorrect options in remainder and LCM problems.

To find the largest n-digit number perfectly divisible by a given divisor D, completely divide the maximum n-digit number (e.g., 999, 9999, 999999) by D and subtract the obtained remainder from it.

Solve the following:

({cosec} 23^circ - sin 23^circ)(tan 23^circ + cot 23^circ)(sec 23^circ - cos 23^circ)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For trigonometric expressions of this form, the result is independent of the angle θ.

Substitute a standard angle, let θ = 45°.

⇒ (cosec 45° − sin 45°)(tan 45° + cot 45°)(sec 45° − cos 45°)

⇒ (√2 − 1/√2) × (1 + 1) × (√2 − 1/√2)

⇒ (1/√2) × 2 × (1/√2) = 2/2 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(cosec 23° − sin 23°)(tan 23° + cot 23°)(sec 23° − cos 23°)

**Formula Used:**

cosec θ = 1 / sin θ, sec θ = 1 / cos θ

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculations:**

Let θ = 23°.

⇒ (1 / sin θ − sin θ) × (sin θ / cos θ + cos θ / sin θ) × (1 / cos θ − cos θ)

⇒ [(1 − sin²θ) / sin θ] × [(sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sin θ × cos θ)] × [(1 − cos²θ) / cos θ]

⇒ [cos²θ / sin θ] × [1 / (sin θ × cos θ)] × [sin²θ / cos θ]

⇒ (cos²θ × 1 × sin²θ) / (sin θ × sin θ × cos θ × cos θ)

⇒ (sin²θ × cos²θ) / (sin²θ × cos²θ)

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Identities

sin θ = 1 / cosec θ, cos θ = 1 / sec θ, tan θ = 1 / cot θ.

Quotient Identities

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.
</p

questions.question: The H.C.F. and the L.C.M. of two numbers are 3 and 672, respectively. If one of the numbers is 96, find the other one.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers equals the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M.

Other Number = (H.C.F. × L.C.M.) ÷ First Number

Other Number = (3 × 672) ÷ 96

Other Number = 2016 ÷ 96 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

L.C.M. of the two numbers = 672

First number = 96

Product of two numbers = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the second number be x.

⇒ 96 × x = 3 × 672

⇒ 96 × x = 2016

⇒ x = 2016 ÷ 96

⇒ x = 21

Product Rule for HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is strictly equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This rule does not apply to three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. For any two co-prime numbers, their LCM is directly equal to their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators)
LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators)
</p

questions.question: Four times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 19 years. After 7 years, twice the age of Q will be 47 years less than seven times the age of P at that time. What is the present age of Q (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let present ages be P and Q.

From 1st condition: 4P − Q = 19 ⇒ Q = 4P − 19

From 2nd condition (after 7 years): 2(Q + 7) = 7(P + 7) − 47

⇒ 2Q + 14 = 7P + 2 ⇒ 7P − 2Q = 12

Substituting Q: 7P − 2(4P − 19) = 12 ⇒ −P = −26 ⇒ P = 26

**∴ The correct answer is 85 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 19 years.

After 7 years, twice the age of Q will be 47 years less than seven times the age of P at that time.

 
 
 Present Ages
 P and Q
 4P − Q = 19

 
 
• 
 

 +7 Years

 
 
 Future Ages
 P+7 and Q+7
 7(P+7) − 2(Q+7) = 47

 
 Solve for Q → Q = 85

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of P = P years

Let the present age of Q = Q years

According to the first condition:

⇒ 4P − Q = 19

⇒ Q = 4P − 19 ---- (Equation 1)

According to the second condition (after 7 years):

Age of P = P + 7

Age of Q = Q + 7

⇒ 2 × (Q + 7) = 7 × (P + 7) − 47

⇒ 2Q + 14 = 7P + 49 − 47

⇒ 2Q + 14 = 7P + 2

⇒ 7P − 2Q = 12 ---- (Equation 2)

Substitute the value of Q from Equation 1 into Equation 2:

⇒ 7P − 2 × (4P − 19) = 12

⇒ 7P − 8P + 38 = 12

⇒ −P = 12 − 38

⇒ −P = −26

⇒ P = 26 years

Now, find the present age of Q by putting P = 26 in Equation 1:

⇒ Q = 4 × 26 − 19

⇒ Q = 104 − 19

⇒ Q = 85 years

**∴ The correct answer is 85 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Present Age Assumption

Always assume the current ages as variables (e.g., x and y) to prevent confusion. Ages 'n' years ago will be (x − n) and 'm' years hence will be (x + m).

Linear Equations in Two Variables

A system of two linear equations like a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 can be easily solved using either the substitution method or the elimination method.

Age Differences Remain Constant

The difference between the ages of two individuals is always the same at any point in time, whether it is evaluated in the past, present, or future.

⇒ 1 + 3/7 = 7/7 + 3/7

It dictates the order of operations in any mathematical expression: Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division & Multiplication (left to right), and finally Addition & Subtraction (left to right).

Reciprocal of a Fraction
